correctness.rationale: The m-th monomial alone has changed squared norm m!(1+τm!), giving e^t−qt^m for t=z conjugate(w), q=τ/(1+τm!). At a fixed radius s the real phase function mθ−s sin θ has largest attained admissible multiple of 2π equal to (m−1)π in the upper half-plane: it is strictly convex, its endpoint values are 0 and mπ, and it increases after the unique crossing in ((m−1)π/m,π). This crossing maximizes the angle among phase candidates and minimizes s^(−m) exp(s cos θ). Since cos θ_m<0 and θ_m increases, C_m decreases strictly from infinity to zero. The scalar modulus equation then excludes every s<r_* and allows exactly the phase-extremal pair at r_*; a multiple scalar root would have to be t=m. Realizability of products precisely for |t|<R² gives the inclusive threshold R²≤r_* for the open bidisk. The strict radial gap follows from C_m(r)>r^(−m) exp(−r). Writing δ=π−θ_m gives mδ+r sin δ=π, so δ=O(r^(−1)) and δ=π/(r+m)+O_m(r^(−3)). Thus log C_m(r)=−r−m log r+π²/(2r)+O_m(r^(−2)). Both defining radii are L−m log L+O_m(log L/L); the mean-value theorem on r+m log r gives the coefficient and stated remainder for their difference. The independent finite bisection/Lambert-W diagnostic at m=3,5,7,9 and τ=10^(−6),0.03,1,200 confirmed the pair and gap in a branch window −8 to 8 (replay: /workspace/branches/695fcd85-98e9-4b08-b4ec-f88e3deb2a28/independent_check.py; output independent_check_results.txt alongside it). It does not establish the all-branch cutoff; the phase comparison does. The frozen script was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: The exact first-zero bidisk is a natural observation-domain invariant for this deformation of the Gaussian kernel. The result shows why the radial estimate is not attained at odd orders, locates the actual critical pair without an arbitrary branch cutoff, and quantifies the leading loss in that estimate as the penalty vanishes. This is a sharp parity-sensitive boundary, not just another Lambert-W notation for the roots.
